G1091370.description: Lingoni is a village on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 2,228.

G1091401.description: Adda-Douéni is a small town on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the town had a population of 6,171.

G921654.description: Wanani (or Ouanani) is a town located on the island of Mohéli in the Comoros. In 2010, it had approximately 2,500 residents.

G921661.description: Vanamboini is a village on the island of Grande Comore in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 1245.

G921664.description: Tsembeho (or Tsémbehou) is a town located on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. it is the third largest city of Anjouan.

G921675.description: Sima is a town located on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. It was the capital of the island during Shirazi rule.

G921721.description: Ouani is a town with a population of over 22,000 people. It is located on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros and is the birthplace of writer Coralie Frei and politician Loub Yacout Zaïdou.

G921726.description: Ongoni is a village on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 1280.

G921729.description: Ntsoudjini is a village on the island of Grande Comore in the Comoros. Its known as the village where the fr:Préfecture d'Itsandra-Hamanvou is located.

G921731.description: Ntsaouéni is a village on the island of Grande Comore in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 2620.

G921745.description: Nyumashiwa (population 3,400) is the second largest city on the Comorian island of Mohéli, after Fomboni, the capital. It is located in the southern part of the island; it is known because of the islets which are in front of the city and which are called the islets of Nyumashiwa.

G921753.description: Mutsamudu (also known as Moutsamoudou) is the second-largest city in the Comoros. It is also the capital and largest city on the island of Anjouan as well the former home of former Comorian president Ahmed Abdallah Mohamed Sambi.

G921762.description: Mrémani is a village on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 3,501.

G921763.description: Mramani (or M'Ramani) is a town located on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. The economy of the city of Mramani is mainly related to local businesses and agricultural crops and local products such as fishing.

G921772.description: Moroni is the largest city, national capital, and seat of the government of the Union of the Comoros, a sovereign archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean. Moroni means "at the river" (mroni in Shingazidja).

G921786.description: Mitsamihuli (population 6,100) is a town on the northwest coast of Grande Comore in the Comoros.

G921806.description: Mbéni is a town located on the island of Grande Comore in the Comoros.

G921814.description: Maraharé is a village on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census the village had a population of 880.

G921834.description: Koni-Djodjo is a town located on the island of Anjouan in the Comoros. The population of Koni-Djodjo is 7,232 inhabitants according to the latest (2002) census.

G921856.description: State on the island of Grande Comore until 1886

G921870.description: Hoani is a town located on the island of Mohéli in the Comoros. Hoani is an internationally significant nesting site for the Green turtle.

G921889.description: Fomboni (population approximately 19,000) is the fifth-largest city in the Comoros. It is also the capital and largest city on the Autonomous Island of Mohéli, of which it makes up more than one third of the population.

G921906.description: Domoni (population 15,351) is the second largest city on the Comorian island of Anjouan in the Indian Ocean and is located on the east coast of the island. It was the capital of the island in the past while the present capital of Anjouan is Mutsamudu.

G921913.description: Djoièzi is a village on the island of Mohéli in the Comoros. According to the 1991 census, the village had a population of 1,636.
